title: Ext finiteness for finitely presented modules with proper support
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], and let $X$ be an algebraic space over $\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-trf-algebraic-space, def-weil-affine-spectrum], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Suppose $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is locally of finite presentation on etale scheme charts [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Let $M,N$ be quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules on the small etale ringed site [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], both of finite presentation, meaning etale locally cokernels of maps $\mathcal O^m\to\mathcal O^n$ with $m,n$ finite. Assume that $N\cong j_*Q$ for a closed immersion $j:Z\hookrightarrow X$ and a finite type quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_Z$-module $Q$, where $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is proper. Here closed immersion is representable and a closed immersion on scheme tests [def-weil-closed-immersion]; finite type for a module means etale locally finitely generated, and proper means separated, of finite type and universally closed on all algebraic-space base changes [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. Use the canonical module direct image [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. Then, for every integer $n\geq0$, the $k$-vector space
$$\operatorname{Ext}^n_{\mathcal O_X}(M,N)
=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_X)}(M[0],N[0][n])$$
is finite dimensional, meaning spanned by finitely many vectors [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The scalar action comes from $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. No properness, separatedness or quasi-compactness of $X$ is assumed.

source.place: Tags 0D0S (lemma-coherent-internal-hom) and 0D0R (lemma-direct-image-coherent-bdd-below), with S=Y=Spec k and proper supports of the cohomology of RHom; proper-support version of the argument of Tag 0D0T (lemma-ext-finite). Finitely presented modules are coherent by spaces-cohomology.tex Tag 07UB (lemma-coherent-Noetherian).

proof.text: Put $Y=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $f:X\to Y$. Every ideal of the field is zero or the whole field, so $k$ is Noetherian. By the definition of local finite presentation, every point of every etale scheme chart $U\to X$ has an affine open neighbourhood $\operatorname{Spec}A$ with $A$ a finitely presented, hence finite type, $k$-algebra. These $A$ are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]; thus each chart is locally Noetherian and $X$ is locally Noetherian. By [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-affine-chart-calculus], the restrictions of $M,N$ to each affine etale chart are associated to finitely presented, in particular finitely generated, modules. This is exactly the coherent-module convention in [lem-sfb-space-coherent-derived-internal-hom]. Thus $M[0],N[0]$ have coherent cohomology, both bounded above and below.

source.place: Tag 07UB (lemma-coherent-Noetherian); spaces-morphisms Tag 04ZK, local Noetherianity checked on charts.

proof.text: Let $G=R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(M[0],N[0])$. Apply [lem-sfb-space-coherent-derived-internal-hom] with $K=M[0]$, $L=N[0]$. Its upper bound on $K$, lower bound on $L$, and local Noetherianity are all supplied by step 1. Consequently $G$ has coherent cohomology and is bounded below. No perfectness or finite projective dimension of $M$ is needed.

Set $T=|j|(|Z|)$. For every etale chart $V\to X$ disjoint from $T$, every chart $W\to Z$ mapping to $V$ is empty. The limit defining $(j_*Q)(V)$ in [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors] is therefore the zero module. Hence $N|_V=0$ on every such scheme chart $V$. By the slice restriction isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction], $G|_V=R\mathcal Hom(M|_V,0)=0$. These charts cover the complement of $T$, so every $\mathcal H^q(G)$ vanishes off $T$. To see that its support $T_q$ is closed, restrict this coherent module to affine etale charts. The comparison of supports in [lem-sfb-space-etale-chart-support] and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-module-support-closed] identify the preimage of $T_q$ with $V(\operatorname{Ann}H_q)$ for the finite chart module $H_q$. The atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology] now makes $T_q$ closed. Since $T$ is the point set of the proper closed subspace $Z$, [lem-sfb-space-proper-support-closed-operations] makes $T$ proper over $Y$, and then makes its closed subset $T_q$ proper over $Y$.

source.place: Tag 0CZE (lemma-closed-closed-proper-over-base); sites-cohomology Tag 08JB (lemma-restriction-RHom-to-U); scheme support Tag 056J (lemma-support-finite-type).

proof.text: The affine scheme $Y$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], and locally Noetherian by its single chart $\operatorname{Spec}k$, hence Noetherian. The map $f$ is locally of finite type, since a finitely presented algebra is finitely generated and the same affine chart neighbourhoods serve; $G$ is bounded below coherent by step 2, and its cohomology supports are proper over $Y$ by step 3. Apply [lem-sfb-space-proper-support-below-coherent-image] to obtain $P=Rf_*G$ with bounded-below coherent cohomology on $Y$. This application uses proper supports, without asserting that $X$ is proper or quasi-compact.

The closed tensor--Hom adjunction of [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal], with symmetry, makes $R\mathcal Hom(M[0],-)$ a right adjoint of $M[0]\otimes^{\mathbf L}-$ as required in [lem-sfb-derived-internal-hom-sections-model]. The latter gives $\operatorname{Ext}^n(M,N)\cong H^nR\Gamma(X,G)$. Let $h:(Y_{\mathrm{et}},\mathcal O_Y)\to(*,k)$ be the global-sections ringed-topos morphism. The canonical direct image $f_*$ of [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors], with $f^{-1}$ and the structure map $f^{-1}\mathcal O_Y\to\mathcal O_X$ used there to define $f^*$, is the module direct image of a ringed-topos morphism, so the $Rf_*$ of step 4 is the one of the next node. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] for $f,h$, one has $R\Gamma(X,G)\cong R\Gamma(Y,P)$ in $D(k)$: its representative comparison is $h_*j$ for a K-injective representative $I$ of $G$ and a resolution $j:f_*I\to J$, and is $k$-linear via the structure morphism. All sites are small in one containing universe.

source.place: Tags 08JA (lemma-section-RHom-over-U) and 0D6E (lemma-derived-pushforward-composition); displayed identities in spaces-perfect Tag 0D0T.

proof.text: Since $P$ has coherent and therefore quasi-coherent cohomology, apply [lem-sfb-affine-etale-derived-module-realization] with $A=k$. Put $E=R\Gamma(Y,P)$. Its equivalence and cohomology compatibility give $a_k(H^n(E))\cong\mathcal H^n(P)$. Coherence on the affine chart $Y$ says that the latter is $a_k(V_n)$ for a finitely generated $k$-module $V_n$. Apply sections and the same node's identity $\Gamma(Y,a_k(V))\cong V$ to obtain $H^n(E)\cong V_n$. The Ext comparison of step 5 respects scalars: on a K-injective target $J$ the multiplication chain map $c\,1_J$, for $c\in k$, acts by postcomposition on the global Hom complex; naturality in the target in [lem-sfb-derived-internal-hom-sections-model] identifies it with multiplication by $c$ on derived global sections. The remaining identifications are in $D(k)$ or are the $k$-linear associated-sheaf and sections comparisons. Thus $\operatorname{Ext}^n(M,N)$ is $k$-linearly isomorphic to $V_n$. The images of a finite generating set of $V_n$ span Ext, as required for every $n\geq0$.
